long_biography.plain_text:
The Royal Ontario Museum’s Crystal bears Michael Lee-Chin’s name in recognition of the investor’s lead gift to its expansion. His C$30 million commitment in 2003 launched the public fundraising campaign. Drawn to the museum’s work across cultures, he saw the contribution as gratitude for the opportunities Canada had given his family. The building’s atrium honours his mother, Hyacinth Gloria Chen.

Lee-Chin’s support for education reflects his own experience of a Jamaican government scholarship that helped him complete engineering studies in Canada. His donation established an institute for corporate citizenship at the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management. Its research and teaching tools help business leaders incorporate sustainability into business strategy.
long_biography.html:
The Royal Ontario Museum’s Crystal bears Michael Lee-Chin’s name in recognition of the investor’s lead gift to its expansion. His C$30 million commitment in 2003 launched the public fundraising campaign. Drawn to the museum’s work across cultures, he saw the contribution as gratitude for the opportunities Canada had given his family. The building’s atrium honours his mother, Hyacinth Gloria Chen.

Lee-Chin’s support for education reflects his own experience of a Jamaican government scholarship that helped him complete engineering studies in Canada. His donation established an institute for corporate citizenship at the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management. Its research and teaching tools help business leaders incorporate sustainability into business strategy.
